correctness.rationale: For any selected t-halfgraph, a rectangle restricts to a subset of a canonical cut C_c because max of its selected row indices is no larger than min of its selected column indices. k<=r cuts leave k+1 gaps; the first row of each gap has all its g edges outside all rectangles, forcing g<=s. Thus t<=k+(k+1)s<=r+(r+1)s. The explicit cut/affine-graph construction realizes equality in a stable semilinear relation. Reversing the inequality and placing cuts every s+1 indices gives the exact inverse cover number. Equality forces k=r, all gaps of length s, and unique cuts; any alternative cut interval would also have to produce this unique optimum, so each actual rectangle has a=b=c. The finite checker independently confirms small cases but is not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The half-graph (ladder) index is a central finite quantitative measure of model-theoretic stability. Rectangular clauses and affine functional exceptional clauses are natural components of stable semilinear relations. The result gives the sharp optimal tradeoff between syntactic rectangle budget r and left-fiber sparsity s, plus its inverse exact matrix covering number and rigidity of extremal decompositions. These interaction and structure results are not supplied by qualitative closure, cannot be obtained merely by relabeling one endpoint bound, and apply to all sets and all nonnegative budgets. The result makes no implausible claim of a general quantitative algorithm for arbitrary stable formulas.
